sentences.text: Onchosaurus is known only from isolated vertebrae and rostral spines.
The genus Onchosaurus was first described by Gervais in 1852.
Based on fossil evidence, Onchosaurus were large, bottom-dwelling fish that inhabited shallow marine environments but were also capable of powerful swimming.
Onchosaurus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae, commonly known as sawskates.
The parent group of the genus Onchosaurus is the family Sclerorhynchidae.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, between 84.9 and 66.043 million years ago.
Its time range spans from the Turonian to the Ypresian stages, approximately 93.9 to 48.07 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in Cretaceous sediments across Egypt, Brazil, Congo, Morocco, France, Niger, Japan, Colombia, Chile, Peru, and the United States.
